interpretation_warning: This is a cross-family inventory, not an assertion that similarly named mechanisms are identical or causally connected.

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which threat increases attachment-system activation, support-seeking behavior samples attachment-figure availability, and the response contributes to distress regulation and later relational expectations.
mechanisms.label: Conditional attachment regulation

mechanisms.definition: Proposed cognitive process that changes the construed meaning of an eliciting situation and thereby changes later emotional responding.
mechanisms.label: Meaning reinterpretation

mechanisms.definition: Proposed context-dependent process in which interpretations, emotions, physiology, behavior, consequences, and beliefs reciprocally constrain future responding.
mechanisms.label: Reciprocal cognitive-behavioral maintenance cycle

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which a new item is analyzed for meaning and related to contextual or existing knowledge, producing a more discriminable later memory representation.
mechanisms.label: Elaborative semantic encoding

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which content-based plausibility and argument-structure information are evaluated concurrently and can support compatible or competing responses.
mechanisms.label: Parallel belief-logic evaluation

mechanisms.definition: Proposed dynamic process in which evaluations of an event's meaning help organize changing action tendencies, physiology, expression, feeling, and action over time.
mechanisms.label: Appraisal-guided component coordination

mechanisms.definition: Proposed learning process in which aversive-outcome omission supports a new memory that reduces conditioned responding when later retrieved.
mechanisms.label: Extinction-memory formation and retrieval

mechanisms.definition: Receptor-linked physiological processes through which glucocorticoid signaling limits or reshapes later HPA secretory activity.
mechanisms.label: Glucocorticoid negative feedback on HPA activity

mechanisms.definition: Proposed action-selection process that uses action-outcome knowledge and current outcome value to guide responding.
mechanisms.label: Goal-directed action control

mechanisms.definition: Proposed cue-linked action-selection process whose momentary expression is relatively insensitive to the current value of the action outcome.
mechanisms.label: Habitual action control

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process by which perceived cardiorespiratory changes are evaluated in a way that can contribute to anxiety experience.
mechanisms.label: Appraisal of cardiorespiratory sensation

mechanisms.definition: Proposed rapid process by which processing a prime makes related target information more available before the target decision without requiring deliberate prediction.
mechanisms.label: Automatic semantic preactivation

mechanisms.definition: Proposed task-sensitive process in which participants predict likely targets or use the detected prime-target relation to influence a decision after target information becomes available.
mechanisms.label: Strategic expectancy or post-lexical matching

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which treatment expectation recruits endogenous opioid signaling that changes pain responding.
mechanisms.label: Endogenous opioid pain modulation

mechanisms.definition: Computational process that updates a value estimate using a prediction-error term and learning-rate parameter.
mechanisms.label: Temporal-difference value updating

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which model exposure supports retention of action-relevant information while observed and direct consequences alter whether and when a matching response is performed.
mechanisms.label: Observation-to-performance selection

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process through which interaction with a familiar support figure changes stress appraisal or regulatory activity and thereby alters physiological responding.
mechanisms.label: Social co-regulation of stress responding

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which allocating attention increases the quality or discriminability of sensory evidence at the attended location.
mechanisms.label: Sensory evidence enhancement at an attended location

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which cue information changes the relative decision weight or criterion assigned to evidence from different locations or intervals.
mechanisms.label: Spatial weighting of evidence for decision

mechanisms.definition: Instrumental learning process in which a response-contingent removal, reduction, or prevention of an aversive consequence increases later probability or rate of the response under relevant conditions.
mechanisms.label: Negative reinforcement learning

mechanisms.definition: Candidate neural computation in which a neuron's stimulus-driven response is divided by a factor that includes pooled activity from other neurons, regulating response gain and saturation.
mechanisms.label: Divisive visual normalization

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process that uses task position information to override a familiar but currently incorrect target response.
mechanisms.label: Control over familiarity-based responding

mechanisms.definition: Proposed process in which retrieval from episodic memory supplies prior-item information used for the current N-back judgment.
mechanisms.label: Episodic retrieval supporting N-back performance
